chapter: Boyhood and the West End camps
title: Birth, family and picking up the trumpet
summary: Born 1907 in the house his father built; nobody in the family played, he took a few school lessons, then played by ear, formed his own band and joined Joe Klessy and Brownlee, learning from Sharkey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: August 23rd, 1907. And where were you born? The house I'm living in now, 2733 Demain Street. Never have moved. Did it belong to your family? My dad built it a year before I was born. Did your dad or your
uncle or grandfather, anybody play music? Nobody in the family played music. I'm the only one in the family. How in the world did you ever get interested?

I don't know. I just saw a horn and liked it, picked it up. I was going to Holy Cross College at the time and got planted by ear. Never did. No, I started to take a few lessons at school. And I wanted to play Dixieland music and the brother wanted me to play march music. So it didn't jive. I quit the class real soon and got to playing by ear, you know. And I formed my own band. After a while I went with Joe Kless's band. From there, Sharky left to go with the Wolverines in New York and Norman Brownlee took me to take his place with Norman Brownlee's band. But I never had any lessons. I just more or less picked what I didn't learn up from Sharky himself.
